PRC Data Challenges

Editions

2

Participating Teams

100+

About

The PRC Data Challenges invite data scientists, researchers, and aviation enthusiasts to tackle real-world aviation performance questions using open data. Organised by the Performance Review Commission (PRC) of EUROCONTROL, each challenge defines a specific prediction or estimation task, provides curated open datasets, and evaluates submissions on a public leaderboard.

A core objective of the PRC Data Challenges is to foster transparency and reproducibility in aviation analytics. All participating teams are required to publish their code in open GitHub repositories, making their methodologies fully inspectable and reproducible. This approach aligns with the PRC’s broader mission to democratise access to performance data and analytical methods, enabling independent validation and building a shared body of open, peer-reviewed techniques for the aviation community.

For more information, visit the PRC Data Challenge programme page.

Challenge Editions

2024 PRC Data Challenge — Actual Takeoff Weight Prediction

Participants predicted the actual takeoff weight (ATOW) of flights using open ADS-B trajectory data, weather information, and aircraft characteristics from a dataset of 369,013 European flights.

Winners (announced at the 12th OpenSky Symposium, Hamburg, November 2024):

Place Team Members Affiliation Country Code
1st likable_jelly R. Alligier et al. ENAC France
2nd tiny_rainbow M. Murca et al. ITA Brazil
3rd brave_pillow A. Tassanbi et al. TU Delft Netherlands

Challenge dataset(s)
How the dataset was built — Journal of Open Aviation Science
Download the dataset — 4TU.ResearchData

2025 PRC Data Challenge — Fuel Flow Estimation

Participants estimated per-second fuel flow along flight trajectories, enabling granular emissions analysis using open data sources. The challenge attracted 179 teams with 2,127 total submissions.

Winners (best RMSE: 200.83 kg/h):

Place Team Members Affiliation Country Code
1st resourceful-quiver M.F. Rahman et al. TU Delft Netherlands
2nd jubilant-vase A. Vernin et al. Sapienza / ENSAI France
3rd outspoken-tornado B. Ryelandt et al. Euranova Belgium

Challenge dataset(s)
How the dataset was built — Journal of Open Aviation Science
Download the dataset — Zenodo
